newsitem.title: USA: Abbott antipsychotic drug seen clearing FDA soon.
newsitem.headline: Abbott antipsychotic drug seen clearing FDA soon.

text.p: A new drug for treating schizophrenia made by Abbott Laboratories Inc is expected to receive marketing approval soon from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, said Wall Street analysts.

Serlect, or sertindole by its chemical name, was once viewed as a potentially major source of future profits for the North Chicago, Ill.-based drugmaker, but its outlook has dimmed following reports of certain side-effects.
"Approval has been expected, but I'm not sure it's going to be a real big deal," said independent analyst Hemant Shah.

An FDA advisory committee met last July and recommended that the agency give final approval to the drug, but at the meeting it was revealed that about four percent of patients in clinical trials with Serlect displayed abnormal heart rhythms.
"There was some concern about potential cardiovascular side-effects," said Cowen & Co analyst Daniel Lemaitre.
Since the panel meeting, Cowen has lowered its Serlect revenue estimate for the year 2000 to $75 million from $300 to $400 million, Lemaitre said.
"We have frightfully small assumptions built into our models because of what happened at that panel," he said.
Key to the FDA approval, if it comes as expected, will be whether the agency requires heart monitoring of patients taking the drug, Lemaitre said.
If so, Abbott may be hard-pressed to market Serlect against rivals with fewer side effects, such as Risperdal from Johnson & Johnson and Eli Lilly and Co's Zyprexa.

"It's certainly not a blockbuster for Abbott. In my mind, it sort of became academic after that panel meeting because it was pretty clear then that this wasn't going to be a huge drug for them," said Wasserstein Perella analyst Robert Dunne.
Two new drugs -- Seroquel from Zeneca Group Plc and Ziprasidone from Pfizer Inc -- are expected to hit the roughly $1 billion market for treating schizophrenia in the next year or so.
